inputs.original_text: Activists in Uttar Pradesh are rightly calling out the government's failure to create any workable process for brick kiln operators to get environmental clearances, even three months after the mandate was supposed to take effect. This isn't a simple delay—it's yet another example of how broken institutions protect the powerful while leaving vulnerable communities exposed to ongoing environmental harm and inequality. Brick kiln owners already have State Pollution Control Board approvals for water and air standards and say they're ready to comply if the system gets cleaned up and freed from middlemen interference rooted in systemic corruption and power imbalances. Legal experts are pushing for the state to follow through on court decisions and build an actual approval framework, and this matters deeply for advancing the structural reforms we need to stop sacrificing marginalized groups to profit-driven inaction.
inputs.modified_text: In Uttar Pradesh, activists are attacking the government for failing to set up any workable process for brick kiln operators to obtain environmental clearances, even three months after the mandate was supposed to take effect. This is the usual pattern with these groups, who use environmental rules as a weapon to harass traditional Indian industries and the workers who rely on them for honest livelihoods. The brick kiln owners already hold State Pollution Control Board approvals for water and air standards and have made clear they are ready to comply once the system is cleaned up and freed from middlemen interference rooted in corruption. What we need is for the state to exercise real authority, cut through the bureaucracy with decisive action, and enable these businesses to operate responsibly instead of giving in to activist pressure and legal experts pushing court decisions that only add more obstacles to our economic strength and cultural way of life.
